name: Tomato Red
lede: Tomato Red is the orange-red of the ripe fruit; as a web color name it is a modern adoption, and its swatch changes from list to list.

sections.title: The fruit, and the web
sections.body:
Paterson defines tomato red as the rich red of the fruit, and notes that it was adopted as an orange-red color name by compilers of web color lists [1]. The X11 set's "Tomato" is #FF6347, a lighter, paler orange-red than this swatch [1]. Our library's own entry, which merges RAL 3013, ISCC-NBS 1955 blocks 11 and 43, Ridgway 1912 and Maerz and Paul 1930, reads darker at #9C322E, close to [[brick]] [2].

The name's age is therefore a matter of which list one trusts. Our library dates it to 1912 via Ridgway's atlas and notes Maerz and Paul's first-recorded year of 1289, a date for a color word that we cannot confirm and treat as unreliable [2]. See also [[tomato]], [[vermilion]] and [[scarlet]] for the same family.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: A color near the library's Tomato Red appears in 12 of 23,781 paintings in our archive, 0.05 per cent, and in 15 by the within-painting reading [3]. In all 15 it plays an accent [3]. The earliest dated match is 1450, 462 years before the name's first record, so it is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph and not a pigment test [3].
